cards.front: What did Hermann Ebbinghaus publish a book about in 1885?
cards.back: His experiments on memory and forgetting.

cards.front: What is the pattern called where a graph shows that memory fades fastest right after learning and the rate of forgetting slows down as time goes on?
What is mistaking ease of reading for real understanding called?

cards.back: Bringing stored information back to mind by yourself.
The research finding that the act of taking a test makes memories stronger.

cards.front: What is the simplest tool for retrieval practice?

cards.back: Spreading total study time across several days leads to better long-term memory than cramming it into one session.
Practicing many problems of the same type in a row, usually grouped by chapter.
Mixing different types of problems together instead of practicing the same type in a row.
Connecting new information to what you already know and explaining it in more detail.
Allan Paivio's idea that memory has separate channels for verbal information and visual information.

cards.front: Why is finding at least one concrete example for each concept useful?
cards.back: It makes the concept easier both to remember and to apply.
The ability to step back and examine your own thinking, having an accurate sense of what you know and what you do not.

cards.front: Which two study techniques did John Dunlosky and his colleagues rate as the most useful methods in 2013?
cards.back: Practice testing (retrieval practice) and distributed practice (spaced repetition).
